style: who is speaking to whom, and what has just happened

candidates.angle: The word parantapa, scorcher of foes, reminds us who is speaking
The word kshatriyam and shudranam split society into four groups
candidates.evidence: ब्राह्मण-क्षत्रिय-विशां (of priests, warriors, merchants) / शूद्राणां (of workers)

candidates.angle: The word svabhavaprabhavaih shows that duties come from nature

angle_hi: परंतप, शत्रुओं को भस्म करने वाले

en.intro: Krishna has just told Arjuna that every being is woven from three qualities. Now he names the four kinds of people who act from those qualities. Listen to how he calls them.
en.notice: Krishna speaks to Arjuna, the warrior, and calls him parantapa, scorcher of foes. In this same breath, he lists the four classes of people, showing that the structure of society is as natural as the qualities that drive it.
en.next: Krishna continues by showing that the natural duty of a brahmin is self-control and knowledge.
en.meaning: O scorcher of foes, the duties of priests, warriors, merchants, and workers are divided according to the qualities born of their nature.

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने अभी अर्जुन को बताया है कि हर प्राणी तीन गुणों से बना है। अब वे उन चार प्रकार के लोगों के नाम लेते हैं जो उन्हीं गुणों से काम करते हैं। सुनिए वे उन्हें कैसे पुकारते हैं।
hi.meaning: हे परंतप, ब्राह्मण, क्षत्रिय, वैश्य और शूद्रोंके कर्म स्वभावसे उत्पन्न हुए तीनों गुणोंके द्वारा विभक्त किये गये हैं।
hi.notice: कृष्ण योद्धा अर्जुन से बात कर रहे हैं और उन्हें परंतप, शत्रुओं को भस्म करने वाले कहते हैं। इसी वाक्य में वे समाज के चार वर्गों का नाम लेते हैं, जो दिखाता है कि समाज की यह संरचना उतनी ही स्वाभाविक है जितने वे गुण जो उन्हें चलाते हैं।
hi.next: कृष्ण आगे बताते हैं कि ब्राह्मण का स्वाभाविक कर्म आत्मसंयम और ज्ञान है।

en.intro: Krishna has just told Arjuna that every being is woven from three qualities. Now he names the four kinds of people who act from those qualities. Listen to how he calls them.
en.body: O scorcher of foes, the duties of priests, warriors, merchants, and workers are divided according to the qualities born of their nature. Krishna speaks to Arjuna, the warrior, and calls him parantapa, scorcher of foes. In this same breath, he lists the four classes of people, showing that the structure of society is as natural as the qualities that drive it. Krishna continues by showing that the natural duty of a brahmin is self-control and knowledge.
